claims.text: The memo's four-era history was researched and corrected in four places, and the corrections are the article.
claims.quote: The research corrected it in four places, and the corrections are the article.

claims.text: The reader did not become the product when the web arrived; the penny press of 1833 made advertising the main revenue and the reader the audience sold to the customer.
claims.quote: The reader stopped being the customer in 1833.

claims.text: In 2005, the best year American newspapers had, advertising brought in $49.4 billion and circulation $10.7 billion, 82 cents of every dollar from the advertiser.
claims.quote: advertising brought in $49.4 billion and circulation $10.7 billion

claims.text: The journalism came from the monopoly, not the model: Lemann's monopoly papers made 20 or 30 percent a year and chose an economically irrational overinvestment in reporting.
claims.quote: an economically irrational overinvestment in reporting

claims.text: Warren Buffett likened owning a monopoly newspaper to owning an unregulated toll bridge every local advertiser had to cross.
claims.quote: owning a monopoly newspaper or dominant market newspaper to owning an unregulated toll bridge

claims.text: The web did not turn readers into a product; it built a second bridge next to the toll bridge, then a third, and the toll went to zero.
claims.quote: It built a second bridge next to the toll bridge, and then a third, and the toll went to zero.

claims.text: Classifieds were about 40% of newspaper revenue and fell from $19.6 billion in 2000 to roughly $6 billion in 2009, with Craigslist alone costing at least $5 billion.
claims.quote: classifieds falling from $19.6 billion in 2000 to roughly $6 billion in 2009

value.unit: billion USD of classified revenue in 2000, down to about 6 in 2009

claims.text: What the newspaper had sold was exclusive attention, and the web has no exclusive.
claims.quote: What the newspaper had sold was not attention but exclusive attention, and the web has no exclusive.

claims.text: Cookies in 1996 and AdSense in 2003 made the reader a product that could be followed, and by 2017 Google and Meta together took 54.7% of American digital advertising.
claims.quote: By 2017 Google and Meta together took 54.7% of American digital advertising.

claims.text: Chartbeat data across 792 news sites shows Facebook referrals down 58% in six years, from 1.3 billion a month to 561 million, and from 30% to 7% of publishers' external traffic.
claims.quote: shows Facebook referrals down 58% in six years, from 1.3 billion a month to 561 million

value.unit: % fall in Facebook referrals to news sites

claims.text: When Canada required platforms to pay for links, Meta blocked news rather than pay; a tenant does not negotiate with a landlord who can turn off the road.
claims.quote: A tenant does not negotiate with a landlord who can turn off the road.

claims.text: In the largest study of its kind, false news on Twitter was 70 percent more likely to be retweeted than true, reached 1,500 people six times faster, and humans not bots did the spreading.
claims.quote: false news stories are 70 percent more likely to be retweeted than true stories are

claims.text: Facebook's own formula weighted every emoji reaction, anger included, at five times a like from 2017, and its data scientists found anger posts disproportionately held misinformation.
claims.quote: weighted every emoji reaction at five times a like from 2017

claims.text: American newspaper newsrooms fell from roughly 71,000 jobs in 2008 to about 31,000 in 2020, a 57% loss.
claims.quote: fell from roughly 71,000 jobs in 2008 to about 31,000 in 2020

claims.text: In Britain at least 293 local newspapers have closed since 2005, and the three largest regional publishers employ about 3,000 journalists against 9,000 in 2007.
claims.quote: at least 293 local newspapers have closed since 2005

claims.text: Provenance is labour, and under both models the hours spent following a claim to its source did not move the click and so were the first to go.
claims.quote: it was the hours that did not move the click and so were the first to go

claims.text: The claim that most provenance work was done in notebooks and spreadsheets is an observation, not a finding; no study counting it was found.
claims.quote: I stand by it as an observation rather than a finding

claims.text: Organic search traffic to publishers fell 33% in the year to November 2025, 38% in the United States, as the search engine began answering the question itself.
claims.quote: fell 33% in the year to November 2025, 38% in the United States

value.unit: % fall in organic search traffic to publishers

claims.text: In Cloudflare's July 2025 data, crawlers fetched 38,000 pages for every visitor Anthropic's sent back, 1,100 for OpenAI's and 195 for Perplexity's.
claims.quote: 38,000 pages for every visitor Anthropic's sent back, 1,100 for OpenAI's, 195 for Perplexity's

value.unit: pages fetched per visitor sent back, Anthropic's crawler

claims.text: In 2021, for the first time in the modern record, circulation revenue overtook advertising, $11.5 billion against $10.3 billion, with advertising down 80% from its peak.
claims.quote: $11.5 billion against $10.3 billion

value.unit: billion USD of circulation revenue against 10.3 of advertising

claims.text: After a century and a half of selling the reader, the industry is selling to the reader again, but as a subscription; it did not go back to 1832, it went to rent.
claims.quote: The industry did not go back to 1832. It went to rent.

claims.text: HTTP/1.1 in 1997 reserved status code 402 Payment Required for digital cash or micropayment systems; it is still reserved for future use and no browser has implemented it.
claims.quote: The web was built with a slot for the creator to be paid, and the slot was left empty for nearly thirty years.

claims.text: DigiCash, the first serious digital cash, filed for bankruptcy in November 1998, and Millicent piloted with 7,000 customers and 24 merchants in 1997 and went no further.
claims.quote: the first serious digital cash, filed for bankruptcy in November 1998

claims.text: Szabo in 1999 and Shirky in 2000 argued that the cost of deciding whether an article is worth two cents exceeds two cents, so people choose the flat fee or the free page.
claims.quote: the cost of deciding whether an article is worth two cents exceeds two cents

claims.text: Neither imagined a buyer with no mental transaction cost at all, which is what an agent with a wallet is, and which is why the argument no longer decides the question.
claims.quote: Neither imagined a buyer with no mental transaction cost at all, which is what an agent with a wallet is

claims.text: Ethan Zuckerman, who invented the pop-up ad, called the fallen state of the internet a consequence of choosing advertising as the default model for online content.
claims.quote: a direct, if unintentional, consequence of choosing advertising as the default model to support online content and services

claims.text: Apple's iTunes store opened on 28 April 2003 selling songs for 99 cents and sold a million in its first week: make the legal way the easy way and people take it.
claims.quote: a million songs sold in the first week

value.unit: songs sold in the first week

claims.text: Substack passed five million paid subscriptions in 2025, four months after passing four million: people paying writers directly, at scale, still as a subscription.
claims.quote: Substack passed five million paid subscriptions, four months after passing four million

claims.text: What has not existed is a way to pay for the thing itself, the fact, the evidence, the confirmation, the projection, rather than a season ticket to the person who produced it.
claims.quote: What has not existed is a way to pay for the thing itself

claims.text: Because the journalism was paid for by a monopoly on distribution, no model that depends on distribution will pay for it again; distribution now belongs permanently to search, platforms and answer engines.
claims.quote: no model that depends on distribution will pay for it again

claims.text: Because the platforms showed that when the reader is measured novelty beats truth, any model that pays for attention will pay for falsehood.
claims.quote: any model that pays for attention will pay for falsehood

claims.text: Stop charging for the road and start charging for the cargo: the story as a graph with every claim walked to hashed evidence, sold in pence on demand, with the money walking back to whoever made the fact.
claims.quote: The fix is to stop charging for the road and start charging for the cargo.
